v1.feedback: The Calder concept genuinely drives the design — palette (vermillion/black/yellow against gold), flat shapes on wires, and the periodic tipping mechanic all read as intentional rather than cosmetic. However, the mobile shapes at 0.2–0.45 radius risk reading as tiny specks at the default camera distance of ~18 units; scale them up 1.5–2× or tighten the FOV so the hanging relationship is legible. Wire opacity at 0.5 may be too faint to establish the 'dangling from' connection that makes a mobile read as a mobile — bump to 0.7 and consider slight per-shape rotation during the tip so flat forms catch directional light differently, reinforcing Calder's kinetic quality.

v2.feedback: The Calder concept is a genuine swerve from the ratatouille parent — flat sheet-metal shapes on wire arms hanging off a differential-growth ribbon is a legit art-historical reference and the palette (vermillion, matte black, cadmium yellow, ivory) is dead-on authentic. The risk is visual clutter: 9 arms with 4 shape types plus the gold ribbon plus fog could read as a decorated Christmas tree rather than a balanced mobile — consider dropping to 5-6 arms with more negative space between them, and making the ribbon itself thinner or semi-transparent so the Calder shapes clearly dominate the composition. The tipping-and-recovery animation is the conceptual heart — if it's too subtle or too fast to read at default camera distance (FOV 34 from z=16), the piece loses its reason to exist; tune the tip amplitude and recovery duration so the off-balance moment is unmistakable at first glance.
